title: The Moon and Sun Pull the Sea Up and Down
description: Why the ocean rises and falls twice a day, explained with NOAA and NASA.
narration: Why does the sea rise and fall twice a day? The Moon has the biggest influence on Earth's tides because it is so close. The distant Sun adds a bit under half the Moon's tide-making pull. Most shorelines see two high tides and two low tides each day. The bulges sit slightly ahead of the Moon instead of right under it. Spring tides happen when the Moon is full or new. Tides are very long-period waves moving through the ocean. The gap in height between high and low tide is called the tidal range.
